title: GS E&C in Talks With KDB as Battery Unit Nears Default - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Energy Materials Halted Pohang Plant Last Month Amid Losses
KDB Can Demand Immediate Repayment of 112.5 Billion Won
Cross-Default Clause Prompts GS E&C to Shift Course GS E&C (006360) has opened talks with the Korea Development Bank to resolve loans owed by Energy Materials, its battery recycling unit now facing default. The trigger is a cross-default clause that could force early repayment of the parent company's foreign-currency bonds if the subsidiary fails to meet its obligations. GS E&C, which had cut off further funding to the unit, is seeking a way to keep the credit risk from spreading to the parent. GS E&C recently began discussions with KDB over 112.5 billion won ($77 million) in outstanding loans owed by Energy Materials, according to industry sources on the 11th. "Simply declaring default would be reckless as a way of running a business," a GS E&C official said. "We will sort this out internally so that it does not happen." A KDB official said the bank is "in discussions to resolve this amicably with GS." Energy Materials, founded in 2020, is 77.65% owned by GS E&C. The company extracts nickel, cobalt and lithium from spent batteries. KDB approved a 120 billion won loan in 2022 to fund construction of the Pohang plant, and Energy Materials had been servicing the principal and interest with money borrowed from GS E&C. But as the slowdown in the electric vehicle market made raw material procurement difficult and plant utilization stalled at around 30%, the Pohang plant suspended operations on the 28th of last month. KDB sent a notice of pending event of default the following day. An EOD allows a lender to demand repayment of the entire loan at once before maturity. That gives KDB the right to claim the full 112.5 billion won balance, effectively the authority to put Energy Materials into default. GS E&C has so far refused to repay the debt directly. The company cites legal risks, including breach of fiduciary duty, if a parent repays debt on behalf of a separate legal entity in the absence of a payment guarantee or debt assumption agreement. An accounting firm review projecting prolonged losses ahead also factored into the decision. Last month, GS E&C stopped extending additional loans to the unit. The cross-default clause emerged as a variable in the process. Foreign-currency bonds worth $30 million, issued by GS E&C headquarters in March last year, carry a clause under which failure by a subsidiary to meet its debt obligations also creates grounds for early redemption of those bonds. If the EOD on the Energy Materials loan is confirmed, an EOD could also arise on the parent company's bonds on or around the 12th. At roughly 40 billion won, the foreign-currency bonds are not an unmanageable amount, but losing the benefit of maturity on parent company bonds because of a subsidiary's troubles could damage GS E&C's credit standing. Financial investment industry observers see the most likely outcome as banks holding the bonds agreeing, after KDB confirms the Energy Materials EOD, to waive application of the cross-default clause. GS E&C has provided a total of 155.9 billion won to Energy Materials to date, including 127 billion won through a rights offering and 28.9 billion won in loans. But as business conditions deteriorated, Energy Materials' net loss widened to 90.9 billion won last year from 32.7 billion won in 2024, and GS E&C booked an 79.9 billion won impairment loss on its stake in the unit last year. Cumulative losses total about 170 billion won. GS E&C put the unit up for sale in August last year but failed to find a buyer. After halting additional loans last month, Energy Materials is now accepting voluntary retirement applications from its roughly 130 employees. The company plans to revive the sale once restructuring is complete. Original reporting by Woo Young-tak for Seoul Economic Daily. AI-translated from Korean. title: GS Caltex Shuts Out Hyundai, Three-Game Skid - 조선일보
content: Silva, Tanacha, Kwon Lead Dominant Victory as Hyundai Engineering & Construction Struggles [Suwon = Sports Chosun Kim Young-rok Reporter] GS Caltex demonstrated the presence of the reigning champion, defeating Hyundai Engineering & Construction and plunging them into a three-game losing streak to start the season. GS Caltex secured a 3-0 (29-27, 25-16, 25-17) victory against Hyundai Engineering & Construction in the 1st Round of the HK Heungkuk Finance 2026-2027 Season V-League Women’s Division, held at Suwon Indoor Gymnasium on the 11th, marking their second win of the season (1 loss). GS Caltex’s triangular trio of Silva, Tanacha, and Kwon Min-ji relentlessly bombarded Hyundai’s court. Their defense featured an impenetrable net-like system, and the attacking line’s problem-solving ability stood out. In contrast, Hyundai Engineering & Construction fell into a three-game losing streak to start the season. Mega showed strong performance in the early stages of the first set but gradually faced concentrated pressure, with her attacks repeatedly blocked in the second set, leading to frustration. Jordan spent more time in the warm-up zone than on the court. Due to frequent lineup changes, the team’s rhythm remained incomplete, and their three-step attacks often failed. Despite Iye-rim’s efforts in both offense and defense, it proved insufficient. Before the match, GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek remained optimistic despite the previous loss to Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK). He emphasized that the team’s attacking power, centered around Silva, remains the best in the league. He expressed particular satisfaction with Tanacha, who joined this year. “Tanacha is full of fighting spirit during training and matches. She creates synergy for the entire team,” he smiled. The outside hitter duo of Tanacha and Kwon Min-ji (both 1m80), who faced Hyundai’s star Mega, also demonstrated top-tier height. Hyundai Engineering & Construction, meanwhile, entered the season with a four-game losing streak, including defeats in the KOVO Cup. Head coach Kang Sung-hyung expressed frustration: “Our reception accuracy and connectivity have been unsatisfactory. This makes it difficult to create synergy to support Mega.” He also mentioned plans to reinforce the middle blocker lineup by utilizing Na Hyun-soo and Kang Seo-woo alongside Bae Yu-na and Kim Hee-jin. The first set decided the match. After a fierce deuce battle, GS Caltex seized momentum, which Hyundai failed to counter. The first set featured a clash between the teams’ star hitters: Silva of GS Caltex and Mega of Hyundai Engineering & Construction. With the score tied at 24-24, confusion ensued as quick attacks, blocks, and service aces alternated. GS Caltex substituted Yu Seo-yeon to shift momentum. At 27-27, Choi Ga-eun’s quick attack and Jordan’s unforced error allowed GS Caltex to claim the first set. The second set was a one-sided bombardment by GS Caltex. Silva dominated early, and as Hyundai adjusted positions, the duel between Silva and Mega intensified. Silva’s height overwhelmed Mega. Tanacha and Kwon Min-ji not only attacked fiercely but also showcased strong defense, leading the team’s momentum. Silva and Tanacha tormented Hyundai with open attacks, quick opens near the net, and feints exploiting gaps. GS Caltex extended their lead early (8-5, 14-9, 19-12) and cruised to victory. In the third set, Hyundai Engineering & Construction briefly led 7-10, but the triangular trio regained momentum to tie at 11-11. Three consecutive unforced errors by Hyundai and a block by Silva allowed GS Caltex to surge ahead 18-12, solidifying their victory and ending the match. title: In professional volleyball, GS Caltex put Hyundai Engineering & Construction in a three-game los.. - 매일경제
content:
In professional volleyball, GS Caltex put Hyundai Engineering & Construction in a three-game losing streak. GS Caltex beat Hyundai Engineering & Construction 3-0 (29-27/25/16/25-17) in the first round of the "HK Heungkuk Finance 2026-2027 V-League" at Suwon Indoor Gymnasium on the 11th. On the day, GS Caltex overwhelmed its opponents in every way. Two pairs of Silva and Tanacha overpowered Hyundai Engineering & Construction with Mega and Jordan, recording an attack success rate of more than 50%. Choi Ga-eun and Kwon Min-ji also helped by scoring double-digit points. Silva scored 7 back attacks, 20 points including 4 blocks, Tanacha scored 12 points, and Choi Ga-eun and Kwon Min-ji scored 11 points side by side. The biggest difference was blocking and error. GS Caltex completely overwhelmed the opponent in the two categories with 11-4 blocking and 10-21 unforced errors. The first set was a close game. GS Caltex took the lead starting with Kwon Min-ji and Silva's consecutive points at 9-9, but Hyundai Engineering & Construction also did not allow a lead of more than two points. The two teams were in a close race, turning the tables to the 20-point range. Twenty-five points made it difficult to determine the superiority and inferiority. Mega's attack at 24-23 was allowed to touch out after the referee's reading, and the game led to deuce. It was a mistake to decide the outcome. At 27-27, Choi Ga-eun's fastball score gave GS Caltex a chance to finish the set, and Jordan's open attack escaped from Hyundai Engineering & Construction's ensuing attack and the set ended as it was. Hyundai E&C players insisted on a touchout, but the referee's video review confirmed that Jordan's ball flew over the opponent blocker Choi Ga-eun's hand. GS Caltex, which had an advantageous position, easily won the set 25-15 after leading early in the second quarter. Silva's performance stood out. He accumulated points by adding smart consecutive hitting attacks to blocking. Silva was active in the second set alone, scoring eight points, including two back attacks and three blocks, with an attack success rate of 62.5%. On the bench of Hyundai Engineering & Construction, as the score at the beginning of the set was 3-6, I tried to call the operation time to break the flow, but to no avail. When calling for the second technical operation time, it was 16-9. At the end of the set, the concentration was disrupted and mistakes continued. Coach Kang Sung-hyung put his hands on his waist and looked at the court without saying anything. Hyundai Engineering & Construction made the change by starting Kang Seo-woo, Lee Chae-young and Kim Hee-jin without Lee Ye-rim, Na Hyun-soo and Bae Yu-na in the third set. This change worked. Lee Chae-young and Kim Hee-jin helped as serve ace, and Jordan and Mega's attacks revived and led 10-7. GS Caltex faced an unexpected variable. Silva, the main scorer, twisted his body trying to catch Han Soo-jin's ball when it was a bit long in a 10-9 situation. Silva went ahead with his appearance, but he didn't have much of an attack in a while. Other players did it instead. Tanacha and Kwon Min-ji scored consecutive points to ease the burden. On top of that, Hyundai Engineering & Construction also made mistakes and lightened their shoulders. Starting with Kang Seo-woo's quick attack and Lee Young-joo's set mistake in the 12-12 tie, he scored five consecutive points to take the mood. It was too much for Hyundai Engineering & Construction to reverse this. In Hyundai Gunseul, Mega fought hard with 18 points (7 back attacks), but the attack success rate was only 36.59%. There were also five mistakes. LOS ANGELES, Calif. – November 11, 2026 –  GS-JJ, a manufacturer of custom promotional gifts, announced today the launch of an upgraded, standardized “five-step customization process” across its core product lines—including promotional keychains, custom lanyards, and custom pins. Clients can use design tools directly on the platform, obtain instant automated quotes, and confirm designs online—replacing the traditional, manual process of email-based inquiries. title: Want to invest in government bonds? RBI's 6.94% GS 2036 auction opens on November 13: How to apply - Upstox
content: 3 min read | Updated on November 11, 2026, 09:57 IST RBI will auction its 6.94% GS 2036 bond on November 13. Find out how retail investors can apply through RBI Retail Direct, minimum investment and key details. Government of India securities carry no domestic currency credit risk, according to the RBI, but they are subject to market risk. | Image: Shutterstock. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will auction the 6.94% Government of India Security 2036 on November 13, 2026. The government plans to raise ₹34,000 crore through the re-issue, with an option to accept an additional subscription of up to ₹2,000 crore. Individual investors can participate through the non-competitive bidding facility on the RBI Retail Direct platform, with a minimum investment of ₹10,000 in face value. The 6.94% GS 2036 will mature on May 11, 2036. Since this is a re-issue, the auction will be price-based and follow the multiple-price method. Maximum investment: ₹2 crore per investor per security per auction Non-competitive bidding window: 10:30 am to 11:00 am Unlike competitive bidders, retail investors do not have to quote a price or yield. They simply specify the face value they wish to purchase. Allotment takes place at the weighted average price emerging from successful competitive bids. The RBI has provided for up to 5% of the notified amount to be allotted to eligible individuals and institutions under this facility. For this auction, that works out to ₹1,700 crore. After opening the account, they can select the eligible security and submit their non-competitive bid during the specified window on November 13. The minimum bid is ₹10,000 in face value, in multiples of ₹10,000 thereafter. The maximum bid is ₹2 crore per investor per security per auction. The actual payment may differ from the face value because the RBI's calculation includes the indicative price, accrued interest and applicable markup. Not necessarily. The 6.94% is the annual coupon rate, not the actual investment yield. For a face value of ₹10,000, the annual coupon interest is ₹694, generally payable in two instalments of ₹347 each, on May 11 and November 11. The actual yield depends on the auction price. title: Ministry of Science and ICT Probes GS Engineering & Construction Data Breach - 조선일보
content: The Ministry of Science and ICT has launched a mandatory investigation into a hacking incident that occurred in GS Engineering & Construction’s apartment community facility reservation and management system. This marks the first case where the newly established “Intrusion Accident Investigation Deliberation Committee” conducted a mandatory investigation following its review last month. The Ministry of Science and ICT announced on the 11th, “GS Engineering & Construction reported the intrusion incident on the 29th of last month but declined to agree to a Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) investigation, opting to analyze the incident internally.” However, the committee concluded that a mandatory investigation was necessary, considering the scale of the data leak and the sensitivity of the information involved. The committee is a statutory body established to proactively respond to intrusion incidents. Earlier, GS Engineering & Construction confirmed unauthorized external access to its apartment community facility reservation and management system around 10:15 p.m. on October 28 and reported the incident to KISA the following day. The potentially leaked information includes residents’ names, birthdates, mobile phone numbers, genders, email addresses, addresses, passwords, membership numbers, residence types, and whether they are household heads. Administrator IDs, final login IP addresses, and RF card numbers were also among the potentially compromised data. A source from GS Engineering & Construction stated, “The company did not refuse the government and KISA’s investigation but only declined technical support for internal cause analysis and preventive measures.” They added, “We will fully cooperate with ongoing investigations, including KISA’s.”

title: Science Ministry Launches Ex Officio Investigation into Security Incident at GS Engineering & Construction Apartment System - 아시아경제
content:
Science Ministry Launches Ex Officio Investigation into Security Incident at GS Engineering & Construction Apartment System The Ministry of Science and ICT said on November 11 that it would launch an ex officio investigation to determine the extent and causes of the damage from a security incident involving GS Engineering & Construction's reservation and management system for apartment community facilities. This is the first case in which an ex officio investigation has been ordered following deliberation by the Security Incident Investigation Review Committee, a statutory committee established last month under the enforcement of the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection. title: GS E&C Opens Talks With Lenders Over Subsidiary's Default Risk - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Battery Recycler Energy Materials Suspends Plant Amid Losses
State Lender Can Demand Immediate Repayment of 112.5 Billion Won
Cross-Default Clause Prompts GS E&C to Reverse Course According to industry sources on Nov. 11, GS E&C recently opened discussions with Korea Development Bank over 112.5 billion won in outstanding loans owed to the bank by Energy Materials, its battery-recycling subsidiary. "Declaring a default without thought would be reckless from a corporate management standpoint," a GS E&C official said. "We will sort this out internally so that doesn't happen." A KDB official also said, "We are in discussions to resolve the matter amicably with GS." Established in 2020, Energy Materials is 77.65% owned by GS E&C. It extracts nickel, cobalt and lithium from spent batteries. KDB approved a 120 billion won loan in 2022 to fund construction of a plant in Pohang, and Energy Materials has been servicing the principal and interest with money borrowed from GS E&C. But as the slowdown in the electric-vehicle market made raw materials harder to secure and the plant's utilization rate stalled at around 30%, the Pohang facility suspended operations on Oct. 28. KDB sent a notice of pending events of default (EOD) the following day. An EOD allows a lender to demand immediate repayment of borrowed funds before maturity. That means KDB can call the entire 112.5 billion won outstanding, effectively giving it the power to put Energy Materials into default. GS E&C has so far refused to repay the debt directly. It argues that Energy Materials is a separate legal entity and that, absent a payment guarantee or debt-assumption agreement, a parent company repaying the debt on its behalf would carry legal risks such as breach of fiduciary duty. An accounting firm's review projecting prolonged losses ahead also factored into the decision. Last month, GS E&C halted additional lending to the unit. The cross-default clause then emerged as a wild card. A $30 million foreign-currency bond issued by GS E&C's parent entity in March last year carries a clause triggering early redemption if a subsidiary fails to meet its obligations. If the EOD on the Energy Materials loan is confirmed, an EOD could also arise on the parent company's bond around Nov. 12. At roughly 40 billion won, the foreign-currency bond is not an unmanageable sum, but losing the benefit of maturity on parent-company debt because of a subsidiary's troubles could damage GS E&C's credit standing. The financial investment industry sees it as most likely that, after KDB confirms the Energy Materials EOD, the banks holding the bond will consult and grant a waiver on applying the cross-default clause. GS E&C had aggressively nurtured Energy Materials as a new business, providing a total of 155.9 billion won, including 127 billion won through rights offerings and 28.9 billion won in loans. But as conditions deteriorated, Energy Materials' net loss widened to 90.9 billion won last year from 32.7 billion won in 2024, and GS E&C booked an 79.9 billion won impairment loss on its stake last year. Cumulative losses total about 170 billion won. GS E&C put the unit up for sale in August last year but failed to find a buyer. After cutting off additional lending last month, Energy Materials is now accepting voluntary retirement applications from its roughly 130 employees. The company plans to revive the sale once restructuring is complete. Original reporting by Woo Young-tak for Seoul Economic Daily. AI-translated from Korean. title: POSCO, GS partner to supply steel solutions for AI data centers - Chosunbiz
content: POSCO will strengthen its competitiveness in the AI market by partnering with GS Group to supply customized steel for an artificial intelligence data center (AIDC) project. On the 11th, POSCO said it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with GS Group at GS Tower in Gangnam District, Seoul, for strategic cooperation in the AI data center (AIDC) business. POSCO CEO Lee Hee-geun and GS Group Vice Chairman Hong Soon-gi attended the event. Under the agreement, the two companies agreed to work together in the domestic and overseas AIDC fields going forward. POSCO will provide tailored steel solutions from the outset of AIDC projects. Starting at the design stage, it plans to offer end-to-end steel supply chain solutions, including steel specifications optimized for structures and equipment, reviews of processing methods and performance testing, and proactive procurement plans aligned with construction timelines. According to POSCO, shortening construction time is key to profitability in the AIDC business. Because AI infrastructure technology advances so quickly, minimizing construction time allows operators to run the latest computing environment on schedule and maximize investment efficiency by booking revenue earlier. To that end, POSCO plans to apply specialized materials optimized for AIDC buildings and equipment operations to shorten construction time and maximize operating efficiency, including PosMAC, electromagnetic shielding materials, and high-efficiency electrical steel. PosMAC is an ultra-corrosion-resistant alloy-coated steel sheet that can be used for a variety of applications such as interior and exterior building materials and cable trays. It reduces corrosion in cooling systems and exterior materials, improving building durability and cutting maintenance costs. Shielding materials can reduce data processing errors caused by electromagnetic interference and improve server stability. High-efficiency electrical steel boosts the efficiency of transformers and generators. With these AIDC-specialized materials, the goal is to increase building durability while reducing maintenance costs and construction time. In addition, the company will seek to apply large-scale power generation and heating and cooling optimization measures, accumulated through steel mill operations, to AIDC operations. GS Group will lead business planning and power supply. GS Engineering & Construction will handle design and construction, and GS Caltex will oversee liquid cooling and other aspects across AI infrastructure buildout and operations. Through this agreement, the two companies aim to build a track record in constructing and operating large domestic AIDC projects and, by linking their overseas networks, to jointly enter foreign markets with strong AI infrastructure demand, including North America and Asia. "AI data centers are growing explosively and will become a key future market that newly drives global demand for steel and materials," POSCO CEO Lee Hee-geun said. "By combining POSCO's next-generation steel solution capabilities with GS Group's infrastructure value chain, we will secure a firm lead in the global AIDC market." title: Korea Launches First Mandatory Probe Into GS E&C Data Breach - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Builder Declined to Consent to Government Investigation
First Case Under Revised Law The Ministry of Science and ICT said it decided on Nov. 11 to conduct a compulsory investigation to determine the extent of the damage and the cause of the GS E&C breach. GS E&C reported the breach of its apartment community facility reservation and management system to the government on Oct. 29. However, it declined to accept technical support from the ministry and the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA), saying it would analyze the incident on its own. In response, the ministry convened the Breach Investigation Deliberation Committee that day to deliberate on the need for a compulsory investigation. The committee agreed that a government-level probe was necessary given the significance of the case, including the scale of the data leak and the sensitivity of the exposed information. The ministry made the final decision after comprehensively reviewing the committee's findings and the potential for additional damage. The probe is the first compulsory investigation conducted through deliberation by the Breach Investigation Deliberation Committee, which was created when the revised Information and Communications Network Act took effect on Oct. 1. It is significant in that the government can investigate directly — taking into account the severity of an incident and the potential for further damage — even if a company withholds consent on the grounds that it is conducting its own probe. If the ministry determines during the investigation that the incident constitutes a serious breach, it plans to consider forming a joint public-private investigation team following deliberation by the committee. Meanwhile, a GS E&C official said, "We did not refuse the government and KISA investigation; we only declined technical support for our own cause analysis and preventive measures," adding, "We will faithfully cooperate with ongoing investigations, including KISA's." title: GS, POSCO Join Forces on Large-Scale AI Data Centers - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
■ Deeper Cooperation in Infrastructure and Materials Technology
Stable Supply Chains to Shorten Construction Timelines
Both Companies to Tap Overseas Bases to Expand Business GS Group (078930) and POSCO are forming a strategic partnership to target the fast-growing market for artificial intelligence data center infrastructure. The two aim to combine GS's infrastructure capabilities with POSCO's steel materials technology to meet surging global demand for AI data centers. The companies signed a memorandum of understanding on strategic cooperation in the AI data center business on the 11th at GS Tower in Seoul's Gangnam District. About 10 key officials attended the ceremony, including GS Group Vice Chairman Hong Soon-ki and POSCO President Lee Hee-keun. The agreement centers on creating synergies by pairing GS Group's data center construction and operation capabilities and global network with POSCO's high-quality steel materials and technology solutions. Specifically, the two companies agreed to jointly identify solutions that strengthen the long-term operational competitiveness of data centers by linking high-efficiency steel materials with design and cooling technologies tailored to data centers. The targeted gains include lower operating costs, better space efficiency and improved durability of equipment and materials. The companies also plan to use the overseas business networks of GS Global (001250) and POSCO to identify global AI data center development demand early, and to jointly pursue supply of materials and equipment for overseas projects along with related business opportunities. Following the agreement, the two sides will set up a group-level working committee to flesh out detailed cooperation tasks, including building an equipment supply chain, developing technologies and solutions, and jointly addressing overseas projects. GS Group is pushing to build a large-scale AI data center in the Bukpyeong No. 2 General Industrial Complex in Donghae, Gangwon State, led by GS AI Infra, a company dedicated to AI data centers. It plans to complete 1.2 gigawatts of capacity in phases starting in 2028 and to secure an additional 1.2 gigawatts, expanding the total to 2.4 gigawatts. The plan is to maximize synergies by drawing on its power and energy capabilities along with the business foundations of affiliates including GS E&C (006360) for design and construction, GS Caltex for liquid cooling and GS Global for overseas networks. POSCO has designated AI data centers as a key area that will drive future steel demand and is strengthening its capabilities in the business. After setting up a future demand development office this year to find demand in new industries such as AI data centers and power grids, it has been expanding development of high value-added steel materials and solutions ranging from structural materials for data center buildings to equipment for power and cooling systems. title: Is Goldman Sachs an Attractive Investment Option Heading into 2027? - The Globe and Mail
content: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS appears well-positioned heading into 2027, supported by strong investment banking (IB) performance, resilient trading revenues and continued growth in its asset and wealth management business. Improving capital markets activity, healthy dealmaking momentum and increasing demand for alternative investments are expected to support revenue growth and profitability. The company's focus on operating efficiency and disciplined capital management strengthens its long-term growth prospects. However, a potential moderation in merger and acquisition (M&A) activity in 2027, coupled with policy and regulatory uncertainties following the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, could dampen investment banking momentum. Elevated expenses and macroeconomic headwinds pose additional challenges. Given these mixed factors, investors may be wondering whether Goldman is still an attractive investment opportunity heading into 2027 or not. To answer this, let us delve deeper. Goldman continues to benefit from the recovery in global IB activity, supported by increased M&A, initial public offerings, and underwriting volumes. The momentum was also evident in the first nine months of 2026, with IB fees jumping 40% year over year to $9.46 billion. Advisory revenues rose 34% to $4.53 billion, while equity and debt underwriting revenues increased 73% and 29% to $2.19 billion and $2.75 billion, respectively. Looking ahead, Goldman's leadership position and robust deal pipeline bode well for continued growth. The company has maintained its #1 position in announced and completed M&A volumes and equity underwriting year to date, advising on $1.5 trillion in announced M&A transactions. Despite strong revenue generation in the third quarter, management indicated that its investment banking backlog remains robust, supported by sustained client engagement and replenishment in equity underwriting. Management continues to view the capital markets environment favorably, with opportunities arising from strategic dealmaking, technology investments and AI infrastructure financing. Although slower M&A activity in 2027 could constrain advisory fee growth, GS's strong dealmaking franchise and sponsor relationships position it to benefit, potentially cushioning the impacts of weaker overall transaction volumes. Similar to Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan JPM and Morgan Stanley MS could face pressure on investment banking (IB) fee growth amid a potential M&A slowdown in 2027. While softer dealmaking activity may constrain advisory revenues for both banks, rising private equity exits and alternative liquidity transactions could provide some offset. The growing adoption of continuation funds and secondary transactions could create advisory opportunities, particularly for Morgan Stanley. Goldman continues to streamline its operations by exiting non-core consumer banking businesses and strengthening its core franchises. Under CEO David Solomon, the company has been strategically shifting its focus toward Global Banking & Markets (GBM) and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM), wherein it maintains strong competitive advantages and sees opportunities to build more durable revenue streams. In sync with these efforts, in August 2026, Goldman announced an agreement to acquire NEOS Investments, a provider of derivative income exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The acquisition is expected to increase Goldman's global active ETF assets under supervision to more than $90 billion, positioning it among the top eight providers by assets. The company also announced an agreement to acquire LCN Capital Partners, expanding its private real estate investment capabilities. In April 2026, Goldman acquired Innovator Capital Management, strengthening its active ETF offerings. In the same month, it completed the divestiture of its Polish asset management business, Goldman Sachs TFI, to ING Bank Slaski. These initiatives complement its broader efforts to reduce exposure to non-core consumer banking operations, including the transition of the General Motors credit card program in 2025 and the planned transfer of the Apple Card program to JPMorgan. The benefits of Goldman's strategic repositioning are increasingly evident in its financial performance. For the first nine months of 2026, GBM revenues jumped 34% year over year to $41.72 billion, while AWM revenues rose 15% to $13.73 billion. Management highlighted that durable revenues have more than doubled since its 2020 Investor Day and accounted for approximately 45% of the total revenues in the first nine months of 2026. These developments reflect Goldman's progress in building a more diversified earnings base, improving revenue stability and strengthening its long-term growth prospects. Goldman continues to accelerate its firmwide artificial intelligence transformation, focusing on improving productivity, streamlining operations and driving long-term operating leverage. The company is integrating AI across its core businesses, including trading, investment banking, asset management and internal operations, to enhance efficiency and strengthen its competitive position. In July 2026, Goldman's Asset Management unit launched AlphaAI, an AI-focused investment platform designed to capitalize on AI-driven investment opportunities across public and private markets. In May 2026, Goldman partnered with Anthropic, Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman to establish a $1.5-billion AI services venture designed to accelerate AI adoption across portfolio companies. These initiatives underscore the company's efforts to leverage AI for both investment opportunities and operational improvements. At the center of Goldman's transformation are One Goldman Sachs 3.0 (OneGS 3.0) and the GS AI Assistant program. OneGS 3.0 is a multi-year initiative focused on embedding AI into the company's operating model by simplifying workflows, automating processes, modernizing infrastructure and improving data management. Meanwhile, the GS AI Assistant is designed to enhance employee productivity by supporting information analysis, content generation and routine tasks, allowing professionals to focus on higher-value activities and client engagement. During the third-quarter 2026 earnings call, management highlighted significant opportunities arising from growing AI infrastructure investments, particularly increased demand for data centers and computing capacity. Goldman expects its financing, advisory and investment capabilities to position it favorably to capitalize on these opportunities. However, management also emphasized the need for disciplined underwriting and prudent risk management as AI-related financing requirements expand. Goldman's focus on operating efficiency is also reflected in its latest results. In the first nine months of 2026, the company's efficiency ratio improved to 59.4% from 62.1% in the year-ago period, reflecting better operating leverage and aligning with its 60% target. While investments in AI and technology may keep expenses elevated in the near term, continued automation and process improvements could enhance scalability, support revenue growth and strengthen long-term profitability. Goldman maintains a strong balance sheet, supported by robust liquidity and capital levels. Its solid financial position allows the company to return capital to shareholders through share repurchases and regular dividend payments while maintaining sufficient flexibility to support business expansion. As of Sept. 30, 2026, Goldman's deposits totaled $568 billion, up from $558 billion as of June 30, 2026. Unsecured long-term borrowings stood at $352 billion. The company's average global core liquid assets increased to $574 billion in the third quarter from $555 billion in the preceding quarter, providing a substantial liquidity cushion. Meanwhile, its standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 12.4%, 100 basis points above the current regulatory requirement of 11.4%. Following the Federal Reserve's 2026 stress test, GS increased its quarterly common stock dividend by 11% to $5 per share. Similarly, JPMorgan announced a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share in September. Morgan Stanley increased its quarterly dividend by 15% to $1.15 per share in the third quarter of 2026. Coming back to GS, in the first quarter of 2025, the board had approved a share repurchase program of up to $40 billion of common stock. As of Sept. 30, 2026, Goldman had nearly $19 billion worth of shares available under authorization. Supported by robust liquidity, solid earnings generation and capital levels above regulatory requirements, Goldman appears well-positioned to sustain shareholder-friendly capital distributions while pursuing growth opportunities. However, the pace of future buybacks will depend on regulatory capital requirements and business investment needs. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Goldman's 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year growth of 39.3% and 3.4%, respectively. The GS stock currently trades at a discount to the industry. The stock is trading at a forward price/earnings (P/E) of 12.32X, below the industry average of 12.34X. Its peers JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are trading at a P/E of 13.26X and 14.36X, respectively. Shares of Goldman have gained 3.1% year to date, outperforming the industry's 0.6% rise but lagging JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley, which have rallied 6.2% and 5.4%, respectively. Goldman's strong investment banking pipeline, resilient trading performance and growing Asset & Wealth Management revenues support its earnings prospects. AI-driven efficiency initiatives and a solid capital position further strengthen its growth potential and shareholder returns. However, elevated expenses, weakness in fixed-income trading and macroeconomic uncertainties remain concerns. Further an expected slowdown in earnings growth from 39.3% in 2026 to 3.4% in 2027, may limit near-term upside. Courtesy of GS Group GS Group and POSCO will form a strategic partnership in the artificial intelligence (AI) data center market, combining GS Group's expertise in data center construction and operation with POSCO's high-quality steel materials and technological solutions. Through the agreement, the two companies plan to minimize delays in the supply of equipment and materials during the construction of large-scale data centers and optimize material selection and design solutions to shorten construction periods and reduce costs. These efforts are expected to facilitate the early operation of data centers and improve their profitability, GS Group said. The agreement also includes practical cooperation to explore ways to reduce operating costs, improve space utilization and enhance the durability of facilities and equipment to strengthen the long-term operational competitiveness of data centers. The two sides will join efforts for global market entry as well, by leveraging the overseas business networks of GS Global and POSCO to identify data center development demands and jointly explore opportunities to supply materials and equipment for overseas projects. “AI data centers require capabilities from various industries to enable stable power supply, rapid construction and efficient operation,” Hong said. “Through this partnership, we will combine GS Group’s data center development capabilities with POSCO’s world-class materials and solutions to explore new growth opportunities in the global AI infrastructure market.” Lee said AI data centers represent a new growth segment that will drive global demand for steel and materials, adding that the two sides will “establish a strong leadership position in the global AI data center market.” GS Group is currently pursuing a 2.4-gigawatt data center project in Donghae, Gangwon Province, through its subsidiary GS AI Infrastructure. In September, the group announced plans to invest approximately 15 trillion won ($11.23 billion) in the first phase of the project and obtained a construction permit for its first 100-megawatt data center in October. POSCO established a new Future Demand Development Office this year to identify business opportunities in AI data center and power grid businesses. The company is also expanding its development of high-value-added steel materials and solutions for data center applications, ranging from structural components to power and cooling equipment. title: GS Group, POSCO Form 'AI Data Center' Alliance to Target North American and Asian Markets - 아시아경제

GS Group, POSCO Form 'AI Data Center' Alliance to Target North American and Asian Markets GS Group and POSCO have joined forces to tap the artificial intelligence data center (AIDC) market. The two companies plan to combine GS Group's capabilities in building and operating data centers with POSCO's steel materials technology to reduce construction time and costs and expand their business into overseas markets, including North America and Asia. GS Group and POSCO said on the 11th that they had signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on strategic cooperation in the AIDC business at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. About 10 key officials from the two companies attended the signing ceremony, including GS Group Vice Chairman Hong Sunki and POSCO President Lee Heegeun. POSCO President Lee Heegeun (left) and GS Group Vice Chairman Hong Sungi pose for a commemorative photo at a signing ceremony for an MOU on cooperation in the AI data center business at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, on the 11th. GS Group Under the agreement, GS Group will oversee the entire process of developing and operating data center infrastructure, including business planning, power supply, design and construction, and liquid cooling. POSCO will provide steel materials and customized solutions needed to build data centers. The two companies plan to minimize delays in equipment supply and optimize designs and materials to shorten construction periods and reduce costs. GS Group is building a large-scale data center at the Bukpyeong 2nd General Industrial Complex in Donghae, Gangwon Province, through its dedicated subsidiary, GS AI Infra. It plans to complete the facility in phases starting in 2028, with capacity of 1.2 GW, and add a further 1.2 GW in the future to bring the total to 2.4 GW. In September, it announced plans to invest about 15 trillion won in the first phase of the project, and last month it obtained a building permit for its first 100 MW-class data center. GS Group plans to draw on its capabilities in power generation and energy, including GS E&C's design and construction expertise and GS Caltex's liquid-cooling technology, for its data center business. It will also leverage GS Global's overseas network to expand its global operations. POSCO plans to adopt an "EVI (Early Vendor Involvement)" model, moving beyond the conventional approach of supplying steel after data center designs are complete and participating from the initial design stage. It aims to shorten construction periods by recommending steel specifications suited to structures and equipment, reviewing processing methods and performance, and supplying materials in line with construction schedules. Data center construction is expected to use POSCO's PosMAC, a highly corrosion-resistant alloy-coated steel sheet, as well as electromagnetic shielding materials and high-efficiency electrical steel. PosMAC will be used in building interior and exterior materials and cable trays to reduce corrosion and improve durability. Electromagnetic shielding materials will help reduce electromagnetic interference in information technology (IT) equipment such as servers, while high-efficiency electrical steel will be used to improve the energy efficiency of transformers and generators. This year, POSCO established a Future Demand Development Office to identify steel demand in emerging industries, including data centers and power grids. It is also considering ways to apply to data center operations the large-scale power generation and heating and cooling efficiency technologies it has developed through operating steel mills. The two companies plan to expand their business overseas after securing results through cooperation on large-scale domestic data center projects. They will jointly target markets in North America and Asia by leveraging POSCO's global steel supply chain and GS Global's overseas network. To this end, they will establish a working-level council to develop plans for building equipment supply chains, advancing technology, and jointly responding to overseas projects. GS Group Vice Chairman Hong Sunki said, "AI data centers are an area that requires the combined capabilities of various industries to ensure a stable power supply, rapid construction, and efficient operation. Through this cooperation, we will strengthen our business competitiveness and identify new growth opportunities in the global AI infrastructure market." POSCO President Lee Heegeun said, "The rapidly growing AI data center market is a key market of the future that will drive new global demand for steel and materials. By combining POSCO's next-generation steel solutions and design support capabilities with GS Group's infrastructure value chain, we will secure a firm leading position in the global AIDC market." © The Asia Business Daily. title: GS expands as Lotte trims, reshaping Korea’s SSM race with quick commerce gains - Chosunbiz
content: Gs the Fresh widens its lead to 299 stores as franchise-led growth lifts revenue 14.9% and operating profit 159.8% in the third quarter GS The Fresh, the No. 1 player in Korea's supermarket (SSM) sector, has topped 600 stores, while Lotte Super has closed more than 30 locations over the past year. GS The Fresh expanded by leaning on franchises, while Lotte Super focused on profitability by shuttering inefficient stores. On the 12th, the retail industry said GS The Fresh, run by GS Retail(21,900 won ▼ 400 -1.79%), had 608 stores at the end of the third quarter, up 27 from a year earlier (581). By contrast, Lotte Super, the industry's No. 2 by store count, fell from 340 to 309 during the same period, a drop of 31. The gap between the two companies widened from 241 stores to 299. GS The Fresh is scaling up while reducing upfront investment by opening mainly franchise locations. In August, it became the first in the sector to surpass 500 franchise stores, and franchises now account for 83% of all locations. GS Retail has applied the franchise know-how it built with the GS25 convenience store chain to its supermarkets, with headquarters managing assortment and ordering, and is adding stores in residential areas and new towns where there is strong demand for quick, close-to-home shopping. That expansion strategy is feeding through to results. GS The Fresh posted third-quarter revenue of 527.7 billion won, up 14.9% from a year earlier. Operating profit jumped 159.8% to 23.9 billion won, and both revenue and operating profit hit record quarterly highs. Lotte Super, meanwhile, is closing low-margin stores and focusing on boosting the efficiency of existing locations. As of the end of the third quarter, 191 of Lotte Super's 309 stores were directly operated, about 62%. Alongside trimming inefficient outlets, Lotte Super is improving cost competitiveness through integrated purchasing with Lotte Mart. Even with fewer stores, third-quarter revenue rose 6.7% year over year to 334.7 billion won, and operating profit increased 16.2% to 5.7 billion won. Same-store sales grew 10% over the period, seen as a sign that productivity per store improved as underperforming locations were cut. As Lotte Super has reduced its footprint, Homeplus Express has signaled a challenge for the No. 2 spot by keeping the door open to new openings. Homeplus Express now has 282 stores, 27 fewer than Lotte Super's 309. Homeplus Express, acquired in June by NS Home Shopping of Harim Group, is working to normalize product supply and restore same-store sales, while recently strengthening store development capabilities to prepare for expansion in regional markets. Harim Group Chairman Kim Hong-kuk said at the 'NS Food Festa 2026' on the 16th of last month, referring to the store network concentrated in the Seoul metropolitan area and major cities, "We have to go first where customers call us." E-Mart Everyday, No. 4 in the sector, has also returned to store growth. Its network fell from 253 at the end of 2023 to 241 in the second quarter this year, then rose to 248 at the end of the third quarter. Results improved as well: third-quarter gross sales were 399.5 billion won, up 7.7% year over year, and operating profit increased by 1.1 billion won to 11 billion won. One reason SSM operators are again focusing on expanding their networks is the growth of quick commerce (nearby instant delivery). Stores used to rely mainly on walk-in customers, but now brick-and-mortar locations also serve as logistics hubs that ship online orders. A denser store network widens the areas eligible for instant delivery and helps capture online demand. In fact, GS The Fresh's quick-commerce sales in the third quarter jumped 52.2% from a year earlier. Quick commerce accounted for 10.1% of total supermarket sales in the third quarter, up from 7.6% a year earlier, marking its first time in double digits. title: GS E&C Maintains "Highest" Rating in Win-Win Growth Index for Sixth Consecutive Year - 아시아경제

GS E&C Maintains "Highest" Rating in Win-Win Growth Index for Sixth Consecutive Year GS E&C announced on November 11 that it had maintained the highest rating for the sixth consecutive year in the Commission for Corporate Partnership’s Win-Win Growth Index evaluation. Yoon Hong Huh, CEO of GS E&C, delivers opening remarks at the "Grand Partners Fiesta 2026," held on the 12th of last month. GS E&C previously also received the highest rating for the fourth consecutive year in the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport’s evaluation of mutual cooperation among construction companies. The Win-Win Growth Index combines the Commission for Corporate Partnership’s comprehensive evaluation of shared growth with the Fair Trade Commission’s evaluation of compliance with fair trade agreements. It rates and publicly classifies large companies’ shared-growth performance into five categories: highest, excellent, average, below average, and very poor. Companies receiving the highest rating are eligible for benefits including a two-year exemption from the Fair Trade Commission’s ex officio investigations in the subcontracting sector, extra points in the Public Procurement Service’s preliminary qualification review (PQ) for public tenders, and preferential treatment when the National Tax Service selects exemplary taxpayers. GS E&C operates its own shared-growth cooperation programs to establish fair business practices with partner companies and promote sustainable growth. It provides various forms of support that partner companies can see and feel in practice, focusing on four areas: ▲compliance management and the establishment of fair trade practices ▲financial and management support ▲strengthening partner companies’ competitiveness ▲promoting horizontal communication. With safety as its top priority, GS E&C pays industrial safety and health management costs in advance and helps cover the cost of assigning dedicated safety personnel to high-risk construction work. It has also worked to strengthen its partners’ safety and quality capabilities and competitiveness, including by introducing a fair competitive bidding system in 2021 to help them secure reasonable profits and maintain stable operations. GS E&C also continues to provide financial support to help partner companies stabilize their operations and strengthen their competitiveness. Each year, it provides KRW 15 billion in interest-free management support and operates a KRW 30 billion shared-growth fund. It also provides support through an annual KRW 4 billion shared-growth cooperation fund for small and medium-sized partners’ technology and research and development, productivity improvements, workforce development, and training. A GS E&C representative said, "Receiving the highest rating in the Win-Win Growth Index for the sixth consecutive year reflects external recognition of our sustained efforts to grow together with our partner companies. We will continue to foster a business environment in which our partners can fully demonstrate their capabilities and promote sustainable shared growth by establishing fair business practices and strengthening effective support programs." © The Asia Business Daily. title: GS Retail Lifts Product Visibility 3.9-Fold With AI Search Optimization - Seoul Economic Daily
content: GS Retail (007070.KS) said on the 11th that product search visibility rose as much as 3.9-fold after it applied technology developed with startups to expand product exposure in artificial intelligence search. The company held a results-sharing session for the fourth class of its open innovation program, Future Retail, at GS Tower in Seoul's Gangnam district the previous day. The event unveiled results from field trials of AI innovation projects that GS Retail ran with five AI startups over four months beginning in July. One of the main results came from an AI search optimization project at GS Shop. The home shopping unit partnered with the startup SearchOS AI to test technology that raises product visibility in AI search. The two companies optimized information on about 100,000 products for generative AI search environments and produced and published 2,000 pieces of content detailing product features and specifications. In the first and second rounds of testing, product search visibility increased 3.8-fold and 3.9-fold, respectively. GS Shop plans to use the findings to shape its customer acquisition strategy. The company also disclosed results from customer behavior analysis at offline stores. GS25 worked with the startup May-i to install an AI-based customer behavior analysis system at four stores with expanded fresh food sections. The technology gauges how shoppers use a store by analyzing figures such as visitor counts and time spent at display shelves, and accuracy on key evaluation metrics came in above 90%. GS25 plans to apply the analysis to product assortment and store operations. "We will continue to use strong startup technologies to improve the customer experience and strengthen field-driven AI transformation (AX) that translates into tangible business results," a GS Retail official said. In the East, the new-look Philadelphia 76ers seem like they've been playing together for years, as LeBron James and Jaylen Brown have hit the ground running with their new teammates. They're tailed tightly by their offseason trade partners, the Boston Celtics, who seemingly haven't missed a beat with new faces around Jayson Tatum. title: LG Uplus, GS Neotek to Integrate Enterprise Security Platforms - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
content: LG Uplus is pursuing the integration of GS Neotek’s cloud security service, Security Lens, into its enterprise network security platform, U+SASE. The goal is to enable corporate security administrators to monitor the security status of cloud servers, as well as employees’ work devices and access networks, through a single platform. LG Uplus and GS Neotek signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on security business cooperation at LG Uplus’s headquarters in Yongsan, Seoul, on Nov. 9. U+SASE protects employee devices and networks when users access corporate systems or the web. Security Lens checks servers and data within cloud environments for security vulnerabilities and analyzes system logs. It also monitors systems operated in companies’ own data centers. The two companies plan to expand their cooperation to include AlphaKey, an integrated identity management service; U+ Safe AI, which prevents data leakage during AI use; and security threat detection and response services. They also agreed to develop plans for reselling security products and conducting joint sales activities.

NINGBO, ZHEJIANG, CHINA, November 10, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ — When European procurement managers evaluate cleaning appliances for retail shelves, expectations have shifted away from superficial aesthetic appeal toward rigorous safety verification. In home cleaning and textile maintenance sectors, electrical safety, temperature rise control, and mechanical protection have become strict baseline metrics. Buyers no longer select products based solely on suction power numbers; instead, they examine how internal components withstand continuous operational stress. Within this shifting trade environment, Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. (Amare) has established a robust operational foothold by aligning manufacturing precision with international safety expectations. As a specialized enterprise focusing on textile maintenance devices, Amare operates as a China leading carpet spot cleaning machine supplier, addressing the rigorous demands of global distribution networks through systematic quality control. The contemporary supply chain environment places considerable emphasis on verifiable reliability at the factory level. Retailers across Western Europe and North America scrutinize supplier credentials down to individual component tolerances and circuit board layouts. When sourcing a carpet spot cleaning machine, procurement teams look for manufacturers who can demonstrate consistent output without compromising on electrical insulation or thermal management. This operational reality requires production facilities to maintain tight tolerances during plastic injection molding, motor assembly, and wiring harness installation. By integrating advanced testing instruments directly into production lines, manufacturing plants can filter out potential defects before final packaging. The Significance of GS Certification in European Markets Quality assurance frameworks in export destinations rely heavily on recognized third-party safety marks. The GS mark, standing for Geprüfte Sicherheit, represents an authoritative German safety certification recognized throughout the European Union. Tested strictly against European Norm standards by accredited independent testing institutions, this mark verifies that a product meets statutory safety requirements regarding mechanical strength, electrical insulation, ergonomic design, and chemical composition. Although the GS mark is technically voluntary under European product legislation, major German retailers, DIY warehouse chains, and regional distributors treat it as a mandatory prerequisite for market entry. Compared to the CE marking, which relies primarily on manufacturer self-declaration, the GS mark requires factory inspections and independent laboratory testing of physical samples. This distinction makes GS certification a formidable benchmark for overseas suppliers seeking entry into premium retail channels. Retail buyers recognize that products bearing this safety mark have undergone rigorous evaluation regarding potential hazards such as short circuits, overheating, user burns, and toxic material emissions. Consequently, achieving GS compliance transforms a standard household appliance into a trusted consumer commodity. Manufacturers who invest in this certification demonstrate a long-term commitment to consumer protection and regulatory transparency, distinguishing their offerings in crowded retail environments. How Precision Manufacturing Supports GS Compliance Meeting stringent German safety standards requires meticulous attention to engineering and internal component design. At its manufacturing facility in Zhejiang, Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. implements dedicated engineering protocols to ensure that every device meets mechanical and electrical safety requirements. The company’s core product lineup includes versatile 500W spot cleaning units engineered for deep textile extraction. These compact machines utilize proprietary self-developed water pumps and heating elements designed to balance cleaning efficiency with thermal stability during extended operation cycles. To prevent fluid ingress into sensitive electrical compartments, these 500W units feature a deliberate clean and wastewater separation architecture. The dual-tank configuration isolates fresh cleaning solution from extracted wastewater, preventing cross-contamination and reducing the risk of internal short circuits. Furthermore, integrated overflow prevention sensors automatically halt water intake when recovery tanks reach maximum capacity. Motor overheating protection mechanisms monitor operational temperatures in real time, cutting power supply automatically if thermal thresholds are exceeded due to restricted airflow or extended continuous use. Beyond internal fluid dynamics, the structural integrity of the appliance plays a critical role in mechanical safety. Precision metal and plastic molds ensure that housing components maintain exact wall thicknesses and tight assembly clearances. This dimensional consistency eliminates loose panel gaps where moisture or dust could penetrate internal circuitry. Strain reliefs on power cords and secure internal wiring harnesses prevent wire fraying or disconnection under mechanical vibration. By combining robust thermal management, precise fluid isolation, and durable mechanical housing, Amare ensures that its carpet spot cleaning machine achieves the structural reliability necessary to pass rigorous GS laboratory evaluations. A credible safety certification is only as reliable as the manufacturing consistency behind it. To maintain continuous compliance with European standards, export suppliers must implement comprehensive batch tracking and quality traceability systems. In modern factory operations, accountability extends from raw material intake to final packaging and palletization. Each manufactured unit receives a unique laser-etched serial number and production batch barcode, linking the finished appliance to specific material lots, component suppliers, and assembly shift logs. When independent auditors inspect production facilities for GS surveillance audits, they examine these traceability records to verify that mass-produced items match the exact specifications of the original tested prototype. Critical components such as thermostats, power switches, pump motors, and internal wiring cables are sourced from qualified tier-one suppliers with verifiable material test reports. Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. archives all incoming material inspection certificates and end-of-line electrical safety test logs in a centralized digital database. This rigorous documentation process enables channel distributors and retail buyers to trace safety data instantly if quality inquiries arise. If a specific batch requires verification, quality assurance personnel can retrieve electrical insulation test results, high-voltage breakdown test records, and functional test logs within minutes. This level of operational transparency reassures commercial partners that product safety is managed through systematic engineering protocols rather than random spot checks. Such structured traceability reinforces long-term trust between Chinese manufacturing enterprises and international trade partners. title: Learnings from Earnings - Goldman Sachs Asset Management
content:
Third-quarter earnings have so far demonstrated resilience. However, as investors begin to look toward 2027, the reporting season is increasingly distinguishing companies with durable demand, visible returns on investment, and pricing power from those where growth comes at an increasingly high cost. Earnings growth is broadening beyond the small group of companies that have dominated market returns in recent years. Beneath headline figures, this is a much more differentiated season. In our view, strong demand across AI infrastructure and industrial suppliers has not always translated into strong earnings, while impressive beats sometimes proved less impressive on closer inspection. Furthermore, markets are not always rewarding solid fundamentals amid volatility. Positive earnings surprises have received relatively muted reactions, while misses have continued to be punished. We believe it is particularly important to distinguish short-term share-price reactions from the durability of the underlying business. We believe over time, companies that convert demand into sustainable margins and free cash flow, protect pricing power through differentiated offerings, and deliver against credible commitments should be better placed to earn market recognition. Investors increasingly want to understand whether demand can be met and how efficiently it converts into margins, free cash flow and ultimately shareholder returns. AI infrastructure may potentially be the clearest example. Major cloud businesses are collectively running at roughly $440 billion of annualized revenues, with growth exceeding 50% year-on-year, while demand continues to exceed available capacity. Expected capital expenditure among five of the largest AI infrastructure spenders has risen to approximately $1.16 trillion for 2027, compared with roughly $800 billion this year.1 The debate has shifted from the willingness to invest toward the ability to fund, deliver and ultimately monetize that investment. In the financial sector, leadership at one major asset manager noted that they are seeing a genuine shortage of capital for the first time in decades as governments and corporations fund this generational AI buildout, creating potential opportunities to position compute and GPU financing as the next major asset class.2 Across the semiconductor ecosystem, supply remains tight, but scarcity is creating strategic choices, forcing companies to protect long-term customer relationships rather than simply maximizing short-term pricing. Meanwhile, industrial companies are acting as the physical backbone of this buildout. Several building-products and industrial services firms are experiencing exceptionally strong demand, with data-center orders surging.3 Yet, despite massive top-line beats, margin conversion is proving to be the real test. Companies are facing significantly higher input-cost pressures, and gross margins are sometimes missing consensus expectations despite booming revenues. We believe AI is becoming a test not simply of technological leadership, but of capital and operational discipline. Two companies may participate in the same structural growth market but generate dramatically different returns depending on how much they pay for capacity and how efficiently they utilize it. We believe the next generation of AI winners will increasingly be determined by balance-sheet capacity, pricing discipline, and return on invested capital, with companies that successfully convert exceptional order books into clean margin expansions standing to outperform. The consumer story is more nuanced than a simple debate about strength or weakness. Aggregate spending remains healthy, but consumers appear increasingly deliberate about what they buy and what constitutes value. Major payments networks continue to demonstrate healthy aggregates, with one major network reporting US payments volumes up 10% and cross-border spending up 14%, and another reporting global payment volumes up 7%.4 Underneath these healthy aggregates, behavior is changing. Financial institutions note that retail accounts are growing, but trading activity per account has seen a broad-based slowdown. Restaurant businesses are seeing diners protect the core meal while cutting back on alcohol or dessert, and buy-now-pay-later volumes have surged 25%, giving consumers another way to manage cash flow without abandoning purchases.5 There is also evidence of strength at both ends of the spectrum, with value laundry products gaining share for one consumer-goods company, while another is seeing growth in premium toothpaste. The same dynamic is playing out in other sectors. Industrial and materials companies are reporting instances where input cost inflation is slightly exceeding pricing power, potentially creating margin headwinds. With consumers and end-buyers more price-sensitive, we believe companies are increasingly focused on protecting value, meaning the answer is no longer to simply pass input costs through to the customer. We favor companies with multiple levers to solve the value equation and strong internal productivity to absorb input cost pressures, rather than relying on broad-based pricing that could alienate a discerning end-user. At a time when investors are scrutinizing the durability of earnings into 2027 and beyond, contracted demand, backlogs and capacity commitments are becoming potentially more increasingly valuable. One leading memory manufacturer has long-term agreements with 14 major customers covering more than 50% of planned 2027-2028 capacity, creating an unusual degree of visibility for an industry historically characterized by pronounced cycles. Further downstream, cloud providers are reporting order backlogs north of $578 billion, with visibility extending into 2028 and parts of 2029. 6 The phenomenon extends deeply into European and US industrials. One building products company now boasts a $23 billion backlog, giving management greater confidence in delivering double-digit organic growth next year because so much demand is already secured. A European machinery company saw mining equipment orders surge 31%, while a global distributor reported that its US data-center backlog now exceeds $3 billion.7 Not all visibility is equal, however, as contracted revenues differ from capacity reservations, which differ again from order backlogs or management guidance. In our view, strong visibility only creates value if companies can fulfill that demand at attractive margins. For investors the distinction between growth that is forecast and growth that is increasingly underwritten is important. In an uncertain environment, credible visibility into future revenues and cash flows commands an increasing premium. We prefer companies with underwritten growth, expanding structural backlogs, and proven execution capabilities. In technology, we will continue looking beyond AI infrastructure spending toward adoption, monetization and returns, asking whether strong demand can translate into sustainable revenues, margins and free cash flow. In consumer sectors, holiday-sensitive companies may provide further evidence on traffic, promotional intensity and pricing, and whether increasingly selective consumers are responding to affordability initiatives. Recent results suggest that supporting volumes through price investment can come at a meaningful cost to margins. Meanwhile, utilities and energy should provide further insight into the second-order effects of the AI investment cycle, including power demand, funding requirements and capital discipline, while energy companies face continued scrutiny over the balance between reinvestment, balance-sheet repair and shareholder distributions. Overall, we are watching for evidence of durable demand, pricing power, capital discipline, and credible 2027 guidance. With positive surprises receiving relatively muted rewards while misses continue to be punished, the remainder of the season may reinforce the importance of distinguishing between companies delivering growth and those converting it into sustainable returns. 1 Company reports.
